I've been farming this land for 30 years. I know this soil, I know what Quzhou winters do to wheat, and I know my well can handle the dry spells. My land is 6 mu, and I do wheat in winter then maize in summer on the same plots — that's how we've always done it here, and it works.

**My thinking:**

I plant wheat first, in October, on all 6 mu. I'll buy improved seed from the village seed shop — not the fancy hybrid stuff, but the better local variety everyone around here uses, probably Jimai. I've been using rotary tillage after I pull the maize, gets the soil ready fast. I fertilize mostly at the base — put down phosphorus and potassium before planting, then add urea at jointing time. I irrigate three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray herbicide in winter and a fungicide pass in spring when powdery mildew tends to come. Expect around 450 jin per mu, maybe a bit more if spring rains cooperate.

After I harvest wheat in June, I go straight into maize. No time to waste. I use hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958, same as most people in the area. I broadcast some fertilizer before seeding and top-dress nitrogen at the big bell stage. I irrigate if it stays dry — usually twice, maybe three times depending on summer rain. One pesticide pass to handle corn borer and any leaf blight. I do rotary tillage before planting. Yields usually come in around 550 jin per mu.

Two of us in the household — we don't need to push the land too hard, but I still want decent output to sell some. This plan is what I know works on my land.
